title: Ferrari nudges up full-year forecasts after beating consensus in Q3
extract: Ferrari raised its full-year outlook after Q3 results beat expectations; the report also notes strong F80 demand and that planned 2027 production of the Luce is already allocated.

title: Architect creates open-source replacement for VM migration tool VMware has hidden
extract: OpenVDDK is an open-source replacement for VMware's Virtual Disk Development Kit, aiming to keep virtual-disk tooling usable without relying on VMware's now-hidden download.

title: Toyota shows off SoC that stores model weights and its OS on integrated memory
extract: Toyota's new system-on-chip places AI model weights and the operating system in integrated memory, aiming to reduce data movement and latency for physical-AI applications.

title: Forget retraining – AI can now tweak another AI's weights
extract: Researchers describe weight-space programming, a way to adjust an existing model's parameters directly rather than retraining it from scratch, opening another route to tuning and composing AI systems.

title: Open models can do 90 percent of agentic work at a twentieth of the cost of a frontier LLM, Gartner says
extract: Gartner's assessment suggests open models can handle roughly 90% of agentic workloads at around one-twentieth the cost of frontier systems, with orchestration and tooling doing much of the heavy lifting.

title: Max-severity bug in widely used OT programming tool exploited to deliver Linux malware
extract: Attackers are exploiting a critical Node-RED flaw to deliver Linux malware, raising the stakes for industrial and IoT deployments that expose the flow-based automation platform.

title: Cops bust botnet of 1.3M infected Android TV boxes
extract: Law-enforcement action has disrupted a botnet built from roughly 1.3 million infected Android TV devices, a significant takedown in the smart-device malware ecosystem.

title: Token thieves costing companies $100K+ per day in illicit LLM charges
extract: Stolen LLM API credentials are being abused for unauthorised inference at costs reportedly exceeding $100,000 per day for some organisations, highlighting the need to protect model tokens like production secrets.

title: FBI pins $6.3B Binance crypto heist on North Korean hackers
extract: The FBI attributes the massive Binance-linked cryptocurrency theft to North Korean hackers, adding an official attribution to one of the sector's largest cyber heists.

title: GhostBSD 26.2 takes the fright out of FreeBSD with a friendlier installer
extract: GhostBSD 26.2 ships with a more approachable installer and an updated FreeBSD base, aiming to make a desktop-friendly BSD system easier to deploy.

title: OpenAI built itself a new Git backend, too
extract: OpenAI's in-house Pando backend is designed for its enormous monorepo workload, cutting Git push latency by nearly five times while serving vast amounts of repository data.

title: Same fab, different paths: Kioxia and Sandisk diverge on HBF
extract: Kioxia and Sandisk are taking different approaches to high-bandwidth flash, as HBF emerges as a potential new memory architecture for data-intensive AI systems.

title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say
extract: Former and current staff told Reuters that concerns about operational security and internal controls were raised repeatedly, prompting scrutiny of how the AI company protects sensitive systems and information.

title: Anthropic restricts AI bot Claude's ability to clone or decompile specific existing games
extract: Anthropic has added server-side restrictions to Claude Code that block certain attempts to clone or decompile named commercial games, while allowing original projects and user-owned material.

title: Former Sega dev shares Mega Drive archive, including abandoned code for Segapede, Jester and a game starring Tails
extract: Former Sega Technical Institute developer Ken Rose has released source code, design documents and related material for several unreleased Mega Drive projects, including Segapede, Jester and a Tails-led game.

title: Modular retro console Polymega is getting support for the Sega Master System, Mark III and Game Gear
extract: A new Polymega teaser points to support for Sega Master System, Mark III and Game Gear software; the company has not yet confirmed the hardware module details or release timing.

title: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night is getting an AI-free SNES port, and you can play it now
extract: A homebrew developer has produced a playable, AI-free SNES port of Symphony of the Night, translating the PlayStation-era game to Nintendo's 16-bit hardware in an ambitious fan project.

title: MediEvil's AI-free recomp hits version 1.0
extract: The community recompilation of the original MediEvil has reached version 1.0, bringing the PS1 classic to modern PC hardware with compatibility and performance improvements.

title: AYANEO's new AYASpace 2 emulator launcher wants to curate your own personal 'Pocket Museum'
extract: AYANEO's AYASpace 2 adds a Pocket Museum interface for emulated games, organising libraries by platform, era, genre and developer, with convenience features aimed at retro handheld users.

title: After 2 years of sneak peeks, fangame Super Mario & The Rainbow Stars just got a spooktacular second chapter
extract: The long-teased fan-made Mario adventure has released its second chapter, adding a new instalment to a community-built project that has been in development for two years.

title: Thief: The Dark Project Remastered brings its sticky fingers to PC and consoles next month
extract: A remaster of LookingGlass's 1998 stealth classic is heading to PC and consoles next month, with a physical edition already available to pre-order—a welcome return for one of PC gaming's foundational immersive sims.

title: Vintage fun: Prodding AI agents using retro hardware just because you can
extract: A developer has connected vintage DECwriter and Commodore-era hardware to modern AI coding agents, turning a retro terminal setup into a working interface for contemporary tools.

title: Audemars Piguet debuts Supersonnerie trio
extract: Audemars Piguet revisits its signature minute repeater with three new Supersonnerie references across Royal Oak and Code 11.59; the titanium soundboard and case architecture amplify the chime, and the titanium Royal Oak is limited to 50 pieces.

title: Insight: Modern escapement developments, Part I
extract: Part I examines modern revivals and refinements of classic escapements, including detent and Robin-derived designs, with a technical look at efficiency, locking and shock resistance.

title: First look: H. Moser & Cie. drops two heritage models, including a new chronograph
extract: H. Moser & Cie. has unveiled two heritage-inspired watches, including a new chronograph, pairing vintage design cues with the brand's contemporary movement work.

title: Introducing: The sleeker, more compact and more accessible Minase Mastercraft J3 collection
extract: Minase's new Mastercraft J3 collection brings its Japanese case-finishing expertise to a more compact, accessible range, with 37mm and 40mm cases and a Miyota 90S5 automatic movement.

title: Direnzo introduces its first GMT, the DRZ 08 Cosmonaire
extract: Direnzo launches its first GMT watch, the DRZ 08 Cosmonaire, using a Sellita SW330-2 caller-GMT movement in a compact 39mm case.

title: Introducing: Casio expands its mechanical range with the CMK-100 collection
extract: Casio expands its mechanical collection with the CMK-100, pairing a compact titanium case with an automatic movement—an unusual direction for a brand better known for quartz and digital watches.

title: The Rhyl Poster by Tom McCarthy review – is this avant-garde spy drama worth the riddles?
extract: Tom McCarthy's new novel blends spy-fiction intrigue with avant-garde literary puzzles; the review weighs whether the riddles reward the reader.

title: Lords of Serendipity by Randy Boyagoda review – a campus satire for this moment of crisis
extract: Randy Boyagoda's comic campus novel turns contemporary university politics and institutional turmoil into a sharp satire.

title: Sarah J. Maas's Court of Splintered Harmony is the UK's fastest-selling adult fantasy novel
extract: The latest Sarah J. Maas release sold 188,914 UK copies in its first week, setting a new record for an adult fantasy novel and underlining the series' enormous readership.

title: True crime novel about murdered Paris life model wins France's biggest literary prize
extract: Philippe Jaenada's novel revisiting the 1949 murder of a Parisian life model has won the Prix Goncourt, bringing a decades-old case into the literary spotlight.

title: New book celebrating 45 years of the ZX Spectrum smashes all Kickstarter goals, receiving £112,000 in pledges
extract: The ZX Spectrum history book's Kickstarter has cleared all stretch goals and raised more than £112,000, turning a 45th-anniversary tribute into a substantial community-funded project.

title: John Leeson, voice of Doctor Who's K9, dies aged 83
extract: Actor John Leeson, who voiced K9 in Doctor Who for decades, has died aged 83—a notable loss for fans of classic British science-fiction television.

title: Alex Garland's Elden Ring adaptation is on course to be Hollywood's goriest ever fantasy movie
extract: Alex Garland's film adaptation of FromSoftware's fantasy epic is shaping up as an unusually brutal screen version, with production details pointing to a high-gore take on the Lands Between.

title: Dustin Hoffman says filming The Graduate was a 'terrible experience' in new memoir
extract: In his new memoir Look at Me, Hoffman revisits the making of The Graduate and describes filming as a miserable experience, offering a fresh behind-the-scenes account of the 1967 classic.

title: Carrie at 50: Brian De Palma's fiery masterpiece still has the power to shock
extract: A 50th-anniversary look at Brian De Palma's adaptation traces how its slow-burn dread, split-screen finale and Sissy Spacek's performance still make it a formidable horror film.

title: Mum, I'm Alien Pregnant review – slime and silliness in amusing New Zealand comedy horror
extract: The Guardian's review finds plenty of slime and silliness in this New Zealand comedy-horror, a deliberately oddball mix of pregnancy panic and extraterrestrial body horror.

title: The Simpsons' French Homer and Marge voice actors marry in real life
extract: The French voice actors behind Homer and Marge, Philippe Peythieu and Véronique Augereau, have married in real life after decades voicing the couple.

title: Blockhead review – comic thriller turns a struggling novelist into a monster
extract: A comic thriller follows a struggling novelist whose attempt to reinvent himself takes a monstrous turn; the review highlights its darkly funny, genre-bending approach.

title: Lupin is back! Omar Sy is ridiculously watchable and effortlessly charming as a blindingly brilliant thief
extract: Omar Sy returns as Assane Diop in the fourth part of Netflix's French heist series, with the review praising the show's charm, disguises and elaborate thief-versus-detective games.
